answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing work that a randomly selected peer can verify against a public task record; each accepted result is tied to a persistent, stake-backed identity, and a challenge can slash that stake for fabricated evidence. A new identity starts with no weight, so splitting into sybils does not multiply influence. An attacker must fund many identities and produce independently checkable work, risking collateral and paying the real labor cost. An opal shipment logged by cedar cooperatives can anchor one thread of such evidence without making names public.
